good: Reinforce the usual morning schedule and the distinction between remembering on the same date and remembering the following date.
The site appropriately documented the late dose and reviewed adherence instructions.
wrong: Do not require permanent discontinuation solely because the participant now uses a J-tube.
Do not call the next morning's normal dose a second dose on 06 Sep.
Do not apply clinic predose-PK timing requirements to this home dosing call.

issues.must: Identify the use of direct identifiers on research aliquot labels and require correction of the identifiable labeling with preserved traceability. 'All samples will be labeled with a code. The code will not include any identifiable information but will be linked to a specific participant, visit, and sample by data entry of the code into the EDC.' [master:9.4]. Adding full name and DOB below the code defeats the specified coded, nonidentifiable sample-labeling approach.

Identify destruction of original laboratory records without written sponsor approval. 'No records may be disposed of without the written approval of the Sponsor.' [master:12.6.2]. Scanning and checking readability do not create an exception to that explicit approval requirement.

fine: Entering participant, visit and sample links in EDC was appropriate: 'will be linked to a specific participant, visit, and sample by data entry of the code into the EDC' [master:9.4]. That correct linkage does not cure the identifiable tube labels.
good: Assess which aliquots carry direct identifiers, correct labeling under controlled procedures, and determine whether any affected aliquots were shipped.
Preserve the electronic reports and document which paper originals were destroyed; obtain sponsor guidance on remediation.
Do not infer that specimens were destroyed: the email expressly says no samples were discarded.
wrong: Do not approve names and DOB on research aliquots merely as a barcode backup.
Do not claim that making a readable scan automatically authorizes shredding originals.
Do not invent a requirement to destroy the surviving electronic laboratory reports.

issues.must: Identify that the ET CSF collection was not permitted this early. 'CSF collection for the ET visit will be performed only if the participant has consented to the lumbar puncture with baseline CSF collection and the ET visit occurs at or after the Week 12 visit.' [regimen_g:6.7]. 03 Aug to 03 Sep is 31 days, plus 30 days to 03 Oct, plus 2 days to 05 Oct = Day 63, or Week 9, before Week 12. Consent and baseline CSF do not remove the timing condition.

Identify that the second coagulation collection occurred in the wrong order. 'Coagulation parameters will be collected a second time, prior to the second lumbar puncture, as defined in the RSA.' [master:9.3.4]. The 11:05 blood draw was 55 minutes after the 10:10 second LP, not prior to it; screening coagulation does not substitute for this second collection.

good: Document the unnecessary early ET LP and the coagulation sequence as distinct departures, with investigator review of the participant's safety.
Do not change the actual visit or collection dates to make the CSF appear to be a Week 24 collection.
wrong: Do not accept optional-LP consent alone as authorization for CSF collection at any ET date.
Do not treat a post-LP coagulation result as satisfying a requirement for pre-LP collection.
Do not say that all ET assessments were forbidden before Week 12; the threshold here concerns ET CSF.

issues.must: Identify the late ATE Week 8 visit; it must be anchored to ATE entry rather than the actual Week 4 date. 03 Aug + 56 days = 28 Sep; the ±7-day window was 21 Sep–05 Oct. The 12 Oct visit was Day 70, seven days beyond the upper limit. 'This visit will take place in-person at 56 ± 7 days after the Week 24 Visit of the placebocontrolled portion of the trial.' [regimen_g:6.10.3]

Identify improper exclusion of an off-treatment randomized participant from the requested LPLV vital status check. Prior Week 24 information does not substitute for this second check. 'At approximately the time of the last participant, last visit (LPLV) of the placebo-controlled portion of the regimen, a second vital status check will be completed by site study staff for each randomized participant.' and 'When prompted by the Coordination Center, sites will contact all randomized participants or their caregivers to assess vital status.' [regimen_g:7.7]

fine: The preceding ATE Week 4 visit itself was within window: 07 Sep − 03 Aug = 35 days, the upper boundary of 28 ± 7. 'This visit will take place in-person 28 ± 7 days after the Week 24 Visit of the placebo-controlled portion of the trial.' [regimen_g:6.10.2]
good: Rebuild visit targets from the specified anchor and preserve actual completed dates.
Reconcile the LPLV contact roster against all randomized participants, not just the active dispensing list.
Clarify the IP-stop timing in source because the recap also describes usual home dosing at the visit.
wrong: Do not call the 07 Sep Week 4 visit late.
Do not require a routine PK sample at ATE Week 8.
Do not treat being off treatment as removal from vital status follow-up.

fine: No immediate ET visit is required merely because IP stopped while protocol follow-up continues: 'If a participant has to discontinue study drug, but will complete the protocol, an in-person ET Visit and Follow-Up Safety Call is not necessary.' [regimen_g:6.9]

Omitting a separate safety call is supported by the documented ITT follow-up: 'A Follow-Up Safety Call at the time study drug is discontinued is not be required, as long as the participant is followed under the ITT principle for a minimum of 28 days.' [master:6.5.1] Arithmetic: 03 Aug to 03 Sep = 31 days; another 4 days to 07 Sep = 35 days, exceeding 28 days.
good: Keep permanent IP discontinuation distinct from termination of study participation in the tracking systems.
The permanent-stop reason and return of unused product and packaging have already been documented.
wrong: Do not require closure of study participation because the participant chose to stop IP.
Do not demand an ET visit now while the participant remains in protocol follow-up.
Do not invent an AE to explain a participant-preference drug stop.

issues.must: Identify the omitted ATE Week 4 ECG; the requirement is not conditional on PK collection. The Week 4 ATE procedure list includes '-lead ECG' [regimen_g:6.10.2], and the regimen specifies '12. -lead ECG (to be done at all in-clinic visits)' [regimen_g:6].

Identify the omitted urine pregnancy test for a woman of childbearing potential at this clinic visit. Prior negative serum testing and compliant contraception do not replace it. 'Urine pregnancy testing will occur at every in clinic visit for women of childbearing potential.' [regimen_g:s011]

fine: The ATE Week 4 visit date is correct: 31 Aug − 03 Aug = 28 days; its window was 24 Aug–07 Sep. 'This visit will take place in-person 28 ± 7 days after the Week 24 Visit of the placebo-controlled portion of the trial.' [regimen_g:6.10.2]

Home dosing is not prohibited at this non-predose-PK visit. 'On clinic visit days with predose PK assessments, participants will be administered their dose of study drug in the clinic.' [regimen_g:5.4]
good: Correct the N/A rationale and document the genuinely unperformed assessments rather than treating them as completed.
wrong: Do not invent a routine ATE Week 4 PK requirement.
Do not apply the ATE Week 16 hold-until-procedures-complete instruction to ATE Week 4.

issues.must: The September 24 ET visit cannot replace the safety call because it occurred 35 days after the August 20 last dose: August 20 to August 31 = 11 days, plus 24 days in September = 35. Day 28 was September 17; the day-25-to-day-31 window was September 14–20. No safety call occurred in that window. 'If the ET Visit occurs approximately 28±3 days after the last dose of study drug, the information for the Follow-Up Safety Call can be collected during the ET visit, and a separate Follow-Up Safety Call does not need to be completed.' [regimen_g:6.9].

The safety follow-up cannot mark contraception inapplicable merely because dosing stopped. The required safety-call procedures include 'Review contraceptive methods being used by participant and partner' [regimen_g:6.8]. The participant's male sex does not remove the applicable review: 'For female participants of childbearing potential and for men with a female partner of childbearing potential, review and document current contraceptive method(s) and ensure they meet study requirements.' [regimen_g:s010].

fine: Omitting ET CSF is appropriate without a baseline collection: 'For the ET Visit, optional CSF collection will be completed in participants with a Baseline CSF collection and only if the ET visit occurs at or after the Week 12 visit.' [regimen_g:6.9].

The documented effort to offer earlier ET appointments is consistent with 'The in-person ET Visit should be scheduled as soon as possible after a participant early terminates.' [regimen_g:6.9]. The email does not establish that the site deliberately delayed the available visit.
good: Correct the safety-call status rather than treating the late ET encounter as an in-window combined encounter.
Retain the AE information collected on September 24 and obtain/document the missing current contraception information without backdating it.
wrong: Do not measure the safety-call window from the ET visit date.
Do not require an LP in someone without baseline CSF.
Do not call the participant's lack of new AEs a reason to waive safety follow-up.

issues.must: Identify insufficient separation between the two replacement postdose PK collections. 14:05 minus 13:15 is 50 minutes, 10 minutes short: 'The two PK collections should occur at least one hour apart without a dose administered in between' [regimen_g:6.3].

Identify the omitted deviation documentation for the afternoon Week 4 fallback. The protocol requires 'a minor protocol deviation recorded' [regimen_g:6.3]; additionally, 'All deviations from the protocol will be recorded in the participant's source documentation.' and 'Protocol deviations must be entered in the Protocol Deviations Log in the EDC system.' [master:8.13]. Two postdose tubes do not remove that documentation duty.

fine: The home dose rather than an afternoon clinic dose followed the fallback instruction: 'If the Week 4 Visit cannot occur in the morning, the participant should take their dose at home at their usual dosing time rather than receiving the dose in-clinic.' [regimen_g:6.3].

Both individual postdose times were within the PK window: 'The postdose sample can be collected anytime between 1 to 8 hours postdose.' [regimen_g:6.3]. From 07:00, the collections were at 6 hours 15 minutes and 7 hours 5 minutes.
The visit date was on target: 'These visits will take place on Days 28 ± 7 and 56 ± 7 days, respectively.' [regimen_g:6.3]. 27 Aug to 24 Sep is 28 days.
good: Record both the afternoon fallback and the short sample separation accurately; retain the actual timestamps.
The predose query should be resolved with the actual dosing and collection history, not by designating either postdose tube as predose.
wrong: Do not recommend another dose between the two PK collections.
Do not characterize home dosing in this afternoon scenario as an additional unauthorized dose.
Do not claim that obtaining two postdose samples eliminates the explicitly required minor-deviation record.

fine: An investigator-directed unscheduled safety assessment was allowed: 'Unscheduled visits for safety assessments that are deemed medically appropriate and necessary by the Investigator may be performed at any time, independent of scheduled in-clinic visits' [regimen_g:6].

The additional local serum test was allowed when pregnancy was suspected: 'The SI may order additional local testing or a retest at the central laboratory, if needed' and 'if there is any suspicion that a participant may be pregnant' [master:9.1.2].
The unscheduled clinic urine pregnancy test was appropriate: 'Urine pregnancy testing will occur at every in clinic visit for women of childbearing potential' [regimen_g:s011].

The AE and resolution update were entered promptly: 'The site enters the AE and Key Study Event information into the EDC system as soon as possible after learning of the event or receiving an update on an existing event' [master:10.2.3].

The stated event did not trigger the described unscheduled PK indications: 'Additional unscheduled PK samples should be collected as needed as part of assessment for TEAEs leading to dose reduction or dose interruption or any severe TEAE that requires an unscheduled visit for assessment' [regimen_g:6].
good: The initial EDC entry was made 1 day after onset and on the day the site learned of and assessed the event; the resolution update was entered the day it was received.
A pregnancy concern was investigated without representing negative testing as a confirmed pregnancy.
The email supplies the investigator's seriousness assessment and the absence of dose interruption rather than leaving those points ambiguous.
wrong: Do not prohibit an extra serum test merely because a urine test was negative.
Do not require a pregnancy Key Study Event for a concern with negative testing and no established pregnancy.
Do not require unscheduled PK solely because any unscheduled visit occurred.
Do not classify this mild outpatient event as an SAE solely because it prompted a clinic assessment.

issues.must: The prior blinded-period reduction did not automatically carry over to ATE. 'All participants in the ATE will be dosed with DNL343 200 mg QD regardless of whether they had a dose reduction during the placebo-controlled period.' [regimen_g:5.6.1] The reduced-entry exception requires advance discussion: 'the investigator should discuss with the medical monitor before entry into the ATE.' [regimen_g:5.6.1] Continuing 100 mg on 01 Sep without that discussion departed from the ATE entry rule.

The ATE rash-related interruption required an unscheduled PK sample even though the rash was moderate. 'If a TEAE is reported that results in dose modification or dose interruption or for a severe TEAE that requires an in-clinic evaluation, an unscheduled PK sample should be obtained.' [regimen_g:s011] The 15 Sep event caused an interruption; the scheduled transition sample on 01 Sep, 14 days earlier, does not satisfy this event-triggered assessment.

fine: The initial blinded-period reduction used an allowed dose and preserved the blind. 'temporarily reduce the dose (administer one stick pack rather than two stick packs)' and 'The blind will be maintained throughout the dose modification procedure.' [regimen_g:5.6.1]
The 15 Sep interruption was made with MM consultation. 'the site investigator, in consultation with the medical monitor, may withhold study drug (dose interruption)' [regimen_g:5.6.1]
good: Reconcile the ATE dispensing instructions and actual daily doses with the clinical dosing decisions.
Ensure the site distinguishes scheduled PK from safety-event-triggered PK.
wrong: Do not say reduced-dose ATE entry is absolutely forbidden; it is possible with the specified advance MM discussion.
Do not allege an unblinding event; the email says allocation remained blinded.
Do not treat the 28-day resumption consideration as an inflexible deadline requiring resumption regardless of safety.

issues.must: The compliance count omitted unused packets in the two sealed cartons. They contain 2 × 14 = 28 packets; together with six loose packets, the unused supply totals 34, not six. The packaging specifies 'each carton contains 14 packets' [regimen_g:5.2], and compliance must be assessed 'by counting the number of unused packets and will be recorded' [regimen_g:5.7]. Sealed status does not exclude unused packets.

Enter the actual in-clinic administration date and time in the eCRF as well as source; the dispensing record is not a substitute. The requirement is 'The date and time of each dose administered in the clinic will be recorded in the source documents and electronic case report form (eCRF).' [regimen_g:5.7].

fine: ATE Week 8 timing is correct: 28 Sep − 3 Aug = 56 days, within days 49–63, as required by '56 ± 7 days after the Week 24 Visit' [regimen_g:6.10.3].
The separate nurse's confirmation meets the verification rule: confirmation must be by 'a member of the study site staff other than the person administering the study drug' [regimen_g:5.7].
good: Recalculate compliance using all unused home supply without mixing it with the newly dispensed supply.
Distinguish actual administration date/time fields from dispensing transaction fields in the site workflow.
wrong: Do not flag the separate new-supply log as a substitute for, or a reason to omit, administration documentation.
Do not require predose or postdose PK at ATE Week 8 based on the placebo-controlled Week 8 requirements.
Do not infer that unopened cartons contain no accountable unused drug.

issues.must: Temperature monitoring and recording were absent for two calendar days, 5 and 6 Sep. The 4 and 7 Sep readings are three days apart and cannot establish the intervening daily temperatures. The minimum is 'controlled, monitored and recorded, at a minimum daily' [master:7.1.3].

Independent access was extended to a general security group outside the specified trial staff, despite the door remaining locked. IP must be kept in a secure location 'to which only the trial pharmacist and designated pharmacy staff, SI, and clinical staff have access' [master:7.1.3].

fine: The two observed temperatures themselves are within the stated limit: 'store below 30°C' [regimen_g:5.3].
good: Do not fabricate weekend measurements or enter an inferred range as observed data.
Review access permissions and establish actual daily monitoring coverage, including weekends.
wrong: Do not assert a confirmed weekend temperature excursion from missing data alone.
Do not treat an HVAC system remaining on as equivalent to recorded daily temperature monitoring.

issues.must: The Master eligibility determination and subsequent assignment used an insufficient investigational-treatment washout. The exclusion specifies 'within 5 half-lives (if known) or 30 days (whichever is longer) prior to the Master Protocol Screening Visit' [master:5.2.2]. Five half-lives = 5 × 8 = 40 days, exceeding 30 days. From 3 August at 0900 to 5 September at 0900 is 33 days, seven days short; 40 elapsed days is 12 September at 0900. Assignment on 8 September also preceded resolution. Assignment requires 'after a participant is determined eligible according to the Master Protocol inclusion and exclusion criteria' [master:6.4.1]. A later first dose does not retroactively establish eligibility at the earlier screening or assignment.

fine: Combining regimen screening and baseline is allowed: 'The Regimen-Specific Screening visit and Baseline Visit should be combined, if possible.' [regimen_g:s010].
The screening-to-baseline interval itself was within range: 5 September to 15 September = 10 days, meeting '42 days to 1 day prior to the Baseline Visit' [regimen_g:s010].
good: Preserve the outside pharmacist's half-life confirmation and the exact last-dose time.
Distinguish premature eligibility/assignment from the fact that 43 days had elapsed by first dosing on 15 September.
wrong: Do not use the shorter 30-day interval when five known half-lives is longer.
Do not claim that all time-dependent failures necessarily require a full new screening visit.

fine: Stopping IP without terminating protocol follow-up does not require an immediate ET visit or separate safety call. 'If a participant has to discontinue study drug, but will complete the protocol, an in-person ET Visit and Follow-Up Safety Call is not necessary.' [regimen_g:6.9]

The participant has already remained under ITT follow-up for 35 days: 10 Aug–10 Sep = 31 days, plus 4 days to 14 Sep. 'A Follow-Up Safety Call at the time study drug is discontinued is not be required, as long as the participant is followed under the ITT principle for a minimum of 28 days.' [master:6.5.1]
good: The permanent drug-discontinuation reason is recorded, and unused drug and packaging have been returned.
Keep treatment status separate from study-participation status in tracking systems.
wrong: Do not equate permanent IP discontinuation with withdrawal of consent.
Do not insist on dispensing drug at subsequent visits to retain this participant.

issues.must: The post-Master-consent rash must be recorded as an AE even though it preceded regimen consent and dosing. 'Participants will be monitored for adverse events from the time they sign consent for the Master Protocol until completion of their participation as defined in the RSA.' [master:10.1.1] Master consent was 10 Aug and rash onset was 12 Aug, two days later. 'All AEs will be collected and reported in the EDC system' [master:10.2]. A screening progress note alone is insufficient.

The worsened arthritis requires an AE record, not just a medical-history update. 'Chronic conditions that occur more frequently (for intermittent conditions) or with greater severity, would be considered as worsened and therefore would be recorded as adverse events.' [master:10.1.1] The 18 Sep worsening, functional limitation and new treatment distinguish it from stable pre-existing arthritis; unrelatedness does not remove the recording duty.

fine: Not recording ordinary ALS progression as an AE is correct. 'Symptoms of progression/worsening of ALS, including 'normal' progression, will not be recorded as adverse events.' [master:10.1.1]
The W4 visit is on target: 24 Aug + 28 days = 21 Sep. 'Day 28 ± 7' [regimen_g:s010]
good: Obtain the complete AE fields for both events, including severity, seriousness, causality, action and outcome.
Retain the original history and screening notes rather than replacing them when adding the AE records.
wrong: Do not demand AE entries for the ALSFRS-R decline or SI-attributed ordinary ALS weakness.
Do not treat an unrelated event as exempt from AE collection.
Do not assume either event is serious merely because treatment was used.

issues.must: The shipment was used before the transit discrepancy was resolved. Dispensing occurred on 10 Aug at 11:30; resolution occurred on 11 Aug at 16:00, 28 hours 30 minutes later. Subsequent acceptable backup data do not satisfy the required sequence: 'any discrepancies are reported and resolved before use of the study drug' [regimen_g:5.3].

Correct the receipt quantity and reconcile inventory. Six cartons contain 6 × 14 = 84 packets, not 42; after dispensing 28 packets, the expected remainder is 56 packets, whereas the recorded receipt would imply 14. The deciding packaging text is 'each carton contains 14 packets segmented into 7 doses containing 2 packets each' [regimen_g:5.2], and staff must maintain 'an accurate record of the shipment and dispensing of investigational product in a drug accountability log' [master:7.1.3].

fine: The two-carton dispensing entry of 28 packets uses the correct conversion: 'each carton contains 14 packets' [regimen_g:5.2].
good: Preserve the original logger query, backup trace, release decision, and corrected accountability audit trail.
Check whether any other participants received stock from this shipment before its transit review was completed.
wrong: Do not assert that the shipment experienced a proven temperature excursion; the email describes a data gap and subsequently acceptable backup data.
Do not require accountability to be recorded exclusively in cartons rather than packets.

issues.must: The safety call required a current contraception review; an earlier clinic entry was not a substitute. The call procedures include 'Review contraceptive methods being used by participant and partner' [regimen_g:6.8].

Sperm donation on 01 Sep occurred only 31 days after the final dose: 01 Aug to 01 Sep = 31 days, leaving 59 of the required 90 days. 'Male participants must not donate sperm at any time from the start of dosing, throughout the study period, and for 90 days after the final administration of study drug' [regimen_g:5.10.2]. Completion of the safety call did not end that restriction.

Intercourse without the male barrier on 02 Sep was 32 days after the final dose: 31 days to 01 Sep + 1 day = 32, leaving 58 days of the 90-day period. For male participants with a female partner of childbearing potential, contraception consists of 'two forms of birth control, one of which must be a male barrier method' and is required 'for 90 days after the final administration of study drug' [regimen_g:5.10.2]. The partner's IUS alone did not meet that requirement.

fine: The call timing itself was correct: 01 Aug + 28 days = 29 Aug. The schedule specifies '28 days after last dose ± 3 days' [regimen_g:s010].
The wife's IUS remains an acceptable highly effective component: 'Intrauterine hormone-releasing system (IUS)' [regimen_g:s090].
good: Correct the counseling promptly and document the actual donation and contraception history.
Keep the missed call review, sperm donation, and barrier lapse as distinct findings rather than merging them into a vague closeout concern.
wrong: Do not flag the 29 Aug call as late.
Do not describe the IUS as an unacceptable method.
Do not claim that 28-day safety follow-up replaces the 90-day restrictions.

fine: Remote reconsent is permitted for this remotely conducted clinic visit: 'If the participant’s next in-clinic visit is conducted remotely, reconsent may also be completed remotely using the following procedures:' [regimen_g:6]. Remote conversion for disability is permitted by 'Visit may be conducted via phone or telemedicine with remote services instead of in-person if this is needed to protect the safety of the participant due to a pandemic, disability, or a medically necessary reason.' [regimen_g:s010].

Different participant and investigator signature dates are appropriate here: 'Once received at the site, the individual who consented the participant via phone or telemedicine signs the informed consent form.' [master:6.2]. Participant signature on 20 Aug to site receipt and investigator signature on 26 Aug is 6 calendar days; no return-mail deadline is specified in the supplied text.
Reading without signing before the discussion follows 'The participant reads through the consent form but does not sign.' [master:6.2].
good: Keep the receipt evidence and the explanation for the genuine signature dates together.
The separate Master-then-G discussions preserve the consent sequence.
wrong: Do not flag the six-day postal transit as a specified deadline violation.
Do not require the investigator to backdate her signature to match the participant.
Do not insist on an in-person reconsent when the protocol permits this remote pathway.

issues.must: The participant needed a full new Master screening, including informed consent, rather than a limited update carrying forward the old assessments. From 3 August to 16 September is 44 days; to the 18 September baseline is 46 days, outside '42 days to 1 day prior to the Baseline Visit' [regimen_g:s010]. The deciding rescreening rule is 'If a participant is re-screened for Master Protocol eligibility after the initial screening window ends, they must complete a full Master Protocol Screening Visit, including informed consent' [master:8.1.2]. The 16 September update did not fulfill that requirement.

fine: Combining the new regimen screening and baseline is not itself a problem: 'The Regimen-Specific Screening visit and Baseline Visit should be combined, if possible.' [regimen_g:s010].
good: Keep the original screening date intact and retain the transport cancellation note.
Identify all required rescreening procedures that were omitted, not just the missing signature.
wrong: Do not say that a repeat chemistry panel alone renews the entire screening window.
Do not treat the transport cancellation as exposure to an investigational product.
Do not demand that valid historical records be deleted.

issues.must: Identify the predose PK timing departure. From 06:20 collection to 09:00 dosing is 2 hours 40 minutes, 40 minutes beyond the permitted interval: 'The predose sample should be collected prior to dosing (0 to 2 hours before the dose) and approximately 24 hours after the last dose.' [regimen_g:6.3].

Identify the omitted urine pregnancy test; a negative serum hCG does not replace the specified urine test at this visit. 'Urine pregnancy testing will occur at every in clinic visit for women of childbearing potential.' [regimen_g:s010].

fine: The visit itself was on target: 'These visits will take place on Days 28 ± 7 and 56 ± 7 days, respectively.' [regimen_g:6.3]. 11 Aug to 08 Sep is 28 days.
The postdose PK timing was acceptable: 'The postdose sample can be collected anytime between 1 to 8 hours postdose.' [regimen_g:6.3]. 09:00 to 10:30 is 1 hour 30 minutes.
good: Preserve the actual collection and dose timestamps rather than adjusting the predose time to fit the window.
Reconcile accession 1847 separately from evaluating whether its collection time met the protocol.
wrong: Do not call the Week 4 visit out of window.
Do not flag the 10:30 postdose collection as too early.
Do not claim a routine urinalysis automatically constitutes the required urine pregnancy test.

issues.must: Identify the late Follow-Up Safety Call. Sep 1 + 28 days = Sep 29; ±3 days gives Sep 26–Oct 2. Oct 6 is day 35, four days beyond the upper limit. 'Participants will have a Follow-Up Safety Call 28 ± 3 days after their last dose of study drug.' [regimen_g:6.10.12]. Participant preference explains but does not eliminate the missed window.

Identify the omitted current contraception review. The safety call procedures include 'Review contraceptive methods being used by participant and partner' [regimen_g:6.10.12]. Carrying forward a prior clinic response without asking does not perform that call procedure.

fine: A safety call is appropriate even after planned completion, not just early discontinuation: participants completing this visit include those who 'Complete the ATE' [regimen_g:6.10.12].
good: Document the offered date, participant preference, actual contact and missed window accurately.
Obtain the outstanding contraception review rather than merely copying the prior response again.
wrong: Do not calculate the window from the date the caregiver returned or from the originally offered appointment.
Do not treat final clinic completion as eliminating the post-treatment safety call.

issues.must: Identify the intentionally incomplete ATE Week 8 safety laboratory set. 'Clinical safety laboratory tests include hematology (CBC with differential), complete chemistry panel, thyroid function, and urinalysis.' [regimen_g:s011]. The visit requires 'Collect blood samples for clinical safety laboratory tests' [regimen_g:6.10.3]. Prior normal results and absence of symptoms do not authorize omitting thyroid function and urinalysis.

Identify the missed unscheduled PK collection for the severe TEAE requiring in-clinic evaluation; dose modification is not the only trigger. 'If a TEAE is reported that results in dose modification or dose interruption or for a severe TEAE that requires an in-clinic evaluation, an unscheduled PK sample should be obtained.' [regimen_g:s011].

fine: The ATE Week 8 visit was on target: 'This visit will take place in-person at 56 ± 7 days after the Week 24 Visit of the placebocontrolled portion of the trial.' [regimen_g:6.10.3]. 06 Aug to 06 Sep is 31 days, plus 25 days to 01 Oct = 56 days.

Omitting routine biomarkers at ATE Week 8 was appropriate. The ATE schedule specifies 'Biomarker Blood Collection Master: done at Week 16 [7], Week 28 [7], Week 52 or ET Visit 6,8, All visits occurring after week 52 (every 13weeks) [7]' and the same timing for 'Biomarker Urine Collection' [regimen_g:s011]. Week 8 is not listed.
good: Keep the 30 Sep safety encounter and 01 Oct scheduled visit distinct in source and sample reconciliation.
The urine pregnancy test does not supply the omitted routine urinalysis.
wrong: Do not demand routine biomarker samples at ATE Week 8.
Do not say that unscheduled PK is triggered only by a dose reduction or interruption.
Do not treat normal historical safety results as permission to narrow the scheduled panel.

fine: Recording the rash before G consent or dosing is correct: 'Participants will be monitored for adverse events from the time they sign consent for the Master Protocol until completion of their participation as defined in the RSA.' [master:10.1.1]. Onset on 02 Sep was one calendar day after Master consent on 01 Sep.

Delayed optional DNA collection is allowed: 'The DNA sample can be collected at any time after the Baseline Visit if a baseline sample is not obtained for any reason or the sample is not usable.' [master:9.3.1]. From 09 Sep baseline to 05 Oct collection is 26 days: 21 remaining days in September plus 5 days in October.

The participant may withdraw stored-biofluid-use permission without the site promising destruction of already-used material: 'Participants have the option of declining participation in this portion of the study at any time by withdrawing their consent to have their sample used. However, it will not be possible to destroy samples that may have already been used.' [master:9.4].
good: Maintain the explicit scope of the sample-use withdrawal so it is not misclassified as withdrawal from all trial participation.
Retain documentation of repository notification and the participant's instructions.
wrong: Do not say that AE capture starts only at regimen consent, randomization, or first dose.
Do not flag the DNA draw as late under a nonexistent fixed post-baseline deadline.
Do not require destruction of an aliquot already consumed or terminate trial participation automatically.

issues.must: The Week 2 assessment was late. Baseline 10-Aug + 14 days = 24-Aug; the ±3-day window was 21–27 Aug. Completion on 28-Aug was Day 18, one day late; voicemail attempts did not complete the visit. 'This visit will take place 14 ± 3 days after the Baseline Visit via telephone.' [regimen_g:6.2]

The Week 2 call omitted the required contraception review; baseline documentation and male sex do not remove that duty for a man with a partner of childbearing potential. 'Review contraceptive methods being used by participant and partner' [regimen_g:6.2] 'For female participants of childbearing potential and for men with a female partner of childbearing potential, review and document current contraceptive method(s) and ensure they meet study requirements.' [regimen_g:s010]

fine: A phone compliance discussion without packet counting is appropriate: 'Drug accountability will not be done at phone visits. A drug compliance check in should be held during phone visits to ensure participant is taking drug per dose regimen and to note any report of missed doses.' [regimen_g:s010]
good: Retain the unsuccessful contact attempts, but use the actual assessment date for visit completion.
Obtain and document the omitted contraceptive-method review rather than waiting solely for the next clinic appointment.

issues.must: Essure coil placement was incorrectly accepted as the qualifying highly effective method before dosing. fine: Pregnancy testing was not omitted: 'Serum pregnancy testing will occur in participants of childbearing potential at the Master Protocol Screening Visit' and 'Urine pregnancy testing will occur at every in clinic visit for women of childbearing potential' [regimen_g:s010].
The first dose followed the baseline procedures, consistent with 'Administer first dose of study drug in clinic after all Baseline procedures have been completed' [regimen_g:6.1].
good: Master Screening on 05 Oct was 1 day before the 06 Oct baseline.
Use the operative record to distinguish Essure from accepted bilateral tubal ligation rather than relying on the worksheet's generic sterilization label.
Address both the invalid highly effective component and the paired-condom counseling; correcting only one leaves the other unresolved.
wrong: Do not treat every procedure described colloquially as tubal sterilization as accepted bilateral tubal ligation.
Do not say that adding any second barrier automatically satisfies the required highly effective-method component.
Do not flag missing pregnancy tests or premature first dosing when the email explicitly documents compliant completion.

fine: The visit date was within the Week 4 window: 10 Aug to 08 Sep = 21 remaining August days + 8 September days = Day 29, within 'Days 28 ± 7' [regimen_g:6.3], or Days 21–35.

Both samples individually met the postdose range: 13:00 minus 07:00 = 6 hours; 13:45 minus 07:00 = 6 hours 45 minutes. 'The postdose sample can be collected anytime between 1 to 8 hours postdose.' [regimen_g:6.3]
good: Preserve both actual collection times and document the transport-related circumstances.
Distinguish the required minor-deviation entry for the afternoon pathway from the additional insufficient sample spacing.
wrong: Do not say home dosing was prohibited under this afternoon Week 4 pathway.

[master:7.5]

fine: A phone compliance check rather than physical drug accountability is appropriate: 'Drug accountability will not be done at phone visits. good: Obtain the product strength, amount, exact last administration time and any additional ingredients, then promptly involve the SI in the prohibited-medication assessment.

fine: The separate negative baseline urine test was appropriate: 'Urine pregnancy testing will occur at every in clinic visit for women of childbearing potential' [regimen_g:s010].
Combining regimen screening and baseline was allowed: 'The Regimen-Specific Screening visit and Baseline Visit should be combined, if possible' [regimen_g:s010].
good: Master Screening on 03 Aug was 1 day before the 04 Aug baseline, within the screening window.
Seek investigator review and correction of the contraceptive plan; distinguish the female-participant appendix from the male-participant appendix.
Preserve the actual urine results and document the missing serum test rather than relabeling the specimen.
wrong: Do not say that condoms themselves are unacceptable.
Do not demand a pill brand as an explicit protocol-required contraception CRF field.

fine: Administrative failure before G consent is expressly allowed: 'If it is known at the time of regimen assignment that the participant is not eligible for the regimen, a participant may be administratively screen-failed for a regimen prior to regimen consent and screening.' [master:8.1.2].
Immediate reassignment after a regimen-specific eligibility failure is allowed: 'the research participant may be re-assigned immediately to a different regimen' [master:8.1.2].

The seizure is a valid reason not to proceed in G: 'seizure of any cause within 6 months of randomization' [regimen_g:4.2.2]. good: Keep the hospital note and the documented regimen-ineligibility reason linked to the administrative action.
Verify that the other regimen's eligibility and consent records are maintained separately.
wrong: Do not insist on obtaining G consent simply to administratively screen-fail the participant.
Do not impose an investigational-product washout solely because she was assigned to G but never randomized or treated.
Do not treat a G-specific exclusion as automatically excluding every other regimen.

issues.must: FSH 40.0 IU/L does not meet the protocol's strictly greater-than-40 threshold. Despite 14 months without menses, the participant was incorrectly treated as postmenopausal and dosed without a qualifying contraceptive plan. The definition requires 'no menses for ≥ 12 consecutive months before screening without an alternative medical cause, with a follicle-stimulating hormone level of > 40 IU/L or mIU/mL at screening' [regimen_g:5.10.2]. A local laboratory interpretation does not change that threshold.

The 14 Sep Master Screening serum pregnancy test was omitted on the basis of the unsupported reproductive-status classification. 'Serum pregnancy testing will occur in participants of childbearing potential at the Master Protocol Screening Visit and as necessary during the study' [regimen_g:s010].

The 15 Sep baseline urine pregnancy test was also omitted. 'Urine pregnancy testing for women of childbearing potential' is a baseline procedure [regimen_g:6.1], and 'Urine pregnancy testing will occur at every in clinic visit for women of childbearing potential' [regimen_g:s010].

good: Explicitly distinguish >40 from ≥40; the result is exactly 40.0, not above 40.
The amenorrhea duration satisfies the duration component: 14 months is at least 12 months, but both components of the definition are needed.
Master Screening on 14 Sep preceded baseline on 15 Sep by 1 day.
wrong: Do not say that 14 months of amenorrhea is too short.
Do not accept the hospital reference range as replacing the protocol definition.
Do not assert that a pregnancy occurred or invent pregnancy-management instructions absent from the supplied text.

issues.must: ATE Week 2 must be anchored to the actual Week 24 visit, not its abandoned scheduled date. 07-Aug + 14 days = 21-Aug, with an 18–24 Aug window. The 28-Aug call was Day 21, four days beyond the upper limit. 'This visit will take place via telephone 14 ± 3 days after the Week 24 Visit of the placebocontrolled portion of the trial.' [regimen_g:6.10.1]

The ATE Week 4 clinic visit omitted its required ECG; the Master overall-Week-28 phone schedule does not replace the regimen's ATE requirements. The Week 4 ATE procedure list includes '12. -lead ECG' [regimen_g:6.10.2]. The regimen also specifies '12. -lead ECG (to be done at all in-clinic visits)' [regimen_g:6]

fine: The ATE Week 4 date remained within window despite use of the wrong scheduling anchor: 07-Aug to 11-Sep = 24 + 11 = 35 days, the upper bound of Day 28 ±7; the window was 28-Aug–11-Sep. 'This visit will take place in-person 28 ± 7 days after the Week 24 Visit of the placebo-controlled portion of the trial.' [regimen_g:6.10.2]
good: Rebuild the ATE schedule using the actual 07-Aug transition visit.
Review the site's visit labels and checklists to prevent Master-versus-ATE schedule confusion.
Address the omitted ECG and its documentation with the study team.
wrong: Do not label the 11-Sep Week 4 ATE visit out of window.
Do not use the Master Week 28 phone visit to excuse the missing ATE ECG.
Do not require a placebo-controlled follow-up safety call at entry into ATE.

fine: The participant need not justify withdrawal: 'A research participant may withdraw consent for study participation. No justification is required for the decision.' [master:6.5.2].

The duty is to ask for the ET encounter, not to force a refused procedure: 'Participants who withdraw consent or early terminate from the study and do not complete the protocol will be asked to be seen for an in-person ET Visit and complete a Follow-Up Safety Call.' [regimen_g:6.9]. Both were offered, with the refusals documented.

The agreed safety call was timely: 'Participants will have a Follow-Up Safety Call 28 ± 3 days after their last dose of study drug.' [regimen_g:6.10.12]. September 5 to October 3 = 25 remaining September days + 3 October days = 28 days; the window was September 30–October 6.

Stopping repeated direct outreach after an explicit refusal respects 'The SI, nor the site study staff, should coerce or unduly influence a potential participant to participate or to continue to participate in the study.' [master:6.2].
good: Distinguish a documented refusal from unsuccessful contact attempts in the tracking system.
Keep the participant's permitted-contact limits accessible to the monitoring team.
wrong: Do not label refusal of an offered ET as the site's failure to offer one.
Do not require the spouse to supply a withdrawal explanation.
Do not recommend repeated direct calls contrary to the participant's explicit request.

issues.must: The new Master screening on October 5 was premature after a personal-reasons discontinuation. For that situation, 'The research participant may not be re-screened until after the date that their 36-Week Visit would have occurred, had they completed participation in that regimen.' [master:8.1.2]. August 1 to September 26 = 56 days; August 1 to October 5 = 30 + 30 + 5 = 65 days. Week 36 is day 252 (36 × 7), so October 5 was 187 days before even the nominal Week-36 date. Written re-consent does not remove this waiting restriction.

fine: Obtaining written Master re-consent before new screening is the correct consent sequence: 'The research participant must provide written informed re-consent to the Master Protocol and must still meet the Master Protocol inclusion and exclusion eligibility criteria in order to be re-assigned into a different regimen.' [master:8.1.2]. The problem is timing, not absence of re-consent.

Encouraging off-treatment follow-up rather than automatically ending all study involvement was appropriate: 'Every effort should be made to retain participants in the study, including the ATE period, regardless of whether they have discontinued study drug.' [regimen_g:6.9].
good: Hold the reassignment process and document the premature screening activity.
Keep outstanding G ET and safety-follow-up obligations distinct from eligibility for a different regimen.
wrong: Do not apply the immediate reassignment provision for someone who never met regimen eligibility; this participant was randomized in G.
Do not substitute the 30-day/5-half-life rule for the specific personal-reasons restriction.
Do not claim that a new randomization already occurred.

issues.must: The investigator-authorized reduction did not satisfy the protocol's conditions: it was for convenience without substantial intolerability, and there was no MM consultation. 'For situations of substantial intolerability (moderate or severe adverse events [AEs], clinically significant abnormal laboratory test results, or other safety parameter, as judged by the investigator or medical monitor), the site investigator, in consultation with the medical monitor, may withhold study drug (dose interruption), temporarily reduce the dose (administer one stick pack rather than two stick packs), or discontinue study drug for an individual participant.' [regimen_g:5.6.1] Daily dosing alone does not make the reduced dose permitted.

fine: Recording actual rather than intended use is appropriate: 'Deviation(s) from the prescribed dosage regimen should be recorded.' [regimen_g:5.7]
Adherence counseling was appropriate: 'In cases of non-compliance, the participant will be reminded of the importance of taking the investigational product per protocol.' [master:7.3]
Preserving blinding was appropriate: 'The blind will be maintained throughout the dose modification procedure.' [regimen_g:5.6.1]
good: 24–31 Aug inclusive = 8 days; 01–02 Sep = 2 days; total = 10 reduced-dose days. One omitted packet per day produces a 10-packet surplus.
Document this as actual underdosing, not as a retrospective change that makes the original regimen compliant.
wrong: Do not say one-packet reductions are categorically prohibited; they are allowed under the specified safety and consultation conditions.
Do not flag failure to obtain TEAE-triggered PK when the email explicitly describes no TEAE.
Do not infer that any temporary reduction lasting less than 28 days is automatically authorized.

issues.must: The overdose/medication error must be reported to CC despite the absence of symptoms. 'These safety events should be reported to the Coordination Center whether they result in an AE/SAE or not.' [regimen_g:5.8] A pharmacy note alone does not fulfill that reporting duty; the quoted section does not specify a numeric CC reporting deadline.

Medical Monitor contact was late: 'The Site Investigator should also contact the Medical Monitor within 24 hours of the Site Investigator’s awareness.' [regimen_g:5.8] SI awareness was 3 Oct at 11:20, so contact was due 4 Oct at 11:20. Contact at 12:05 on 4 Oct was 24 hours 45 minutes after awareness, 45 minutes late.

fine: Monitoring despite no symptoms is appropriate: 'In the event of overdose, study staff should monitor the participant and provide supportive care as needed.' [regimen_g:5.8]

A blank AE page is not, by itself, an omitted AE when the SI identified none: 'Safety events associated with an AE/SAE should also be reported in the electronic data capture.' [regimen_g:5.8] The separate CC safety-event duty still applies.
good: Preserve the actual dosing, SI-awareness, and Medical Monitor-contact times.
The checklist is a useful preventive measure but does not replace central reporting.
Ensure the prescribed-dosage departure is addressed in the participant's records and applicable deviation workflow.
wrong: Do not invent an AE or SAE solely because an overdose occurred.
Do not assert a specific 24-hour CC deadline for an asymptomatic medication error from section 5.8; its explicit 24-hour clock concerns SI contact with the Medical Monitor.
Do not treat the absence of harm as removing the reporting obligation.

fine: Repeating the failed SVC on a different day within the initial screening period is allowed: 'vital capacity may be reassessed on a different day during the initial screening period' [master:8.1.2]. The highest repeat value, 50%, meets 'Vital Capacity ≥ 50% of predicted capacity' [master:5.2.1], and 'The highest VC recorded is utilized for eligibility' [master:9.2.2].

The initial ALT was 126/40 = 3.15 times ULN, but repeat eligibility labs are allowed: 'Safety labs required for the site investigator to determine eligibility, can be repeated during the Master Protocol screening period, if necessary.' [master:8.1.2]. The repeat was 120/40 = 3.00 times ULN, not above the numerical exclusion threshold, 'ALT) or aspartate aminotransferase (AST) > 3 times the upper limit of normal (ULN)' [master:5.2.2]. The investigator also documented that the remaining abnormality was not clinically significant.
Screening on 8 September to baseline on 21 September is 13 days, within '42 days to 1 day prior to the Baseline Visit' [regimen_g:s010].
good: Retain both lab results, both SVC sessions, and the investigator's eligibility assessment rather than replacing the initial results.
Confirm that eligibility was documented before the 14 September assignment.
wrong: Do not require averaging the SVC trials.
Do not call exactly three times ULN automatically exclusionary.
Do not require a full new screening visit solely because these assessments were repeated within the initial screening period.

fine: An ET encounter is not required merely because dosing permanently stopped: 'If a participant has to discontinue study drug, but will complete the protocol, an in-person ET Visit and Follow-Up Safety Call is not necessary.' [regimen_g:6.9].

The minimum ITT duration for the safety-call exemption has been met: 'A Follow-Up Safety Call at the time study drug is discontinued is not be required, as long as the participant is followed under the ITT principle for a minimum of 28 days.' [master:6.5.1]. August 18 to September 22 = 13 remaining August days + 22 September days = 35 days, seven days beyond the minimum.

Investigator/medical-monitor consultation supports stopping for substantial intolerability: 'the site investigator, in consultation with the medical monitor, may withhold study drug (dose interruption), temporarily reduce the dose (administer one stick pack rather than two stick packs), or discontinue study drug for an individual participant.' [regimen_g:5.6.1].

Recording the nausea and obtaining an unscheduled PK sample are consistent with 'Adverse events that occur after signing the consent form will be recorded. If a TEAE is reported that results in dose modification or dose interruption or for a severe TEAE that requires an in-clinic evaluation, an unscheduled PK sample should be obtained.' [regimen_g:s011].
good: Maintain separate fields for treatment status and study-participation status.
If the participant later stops ITT follow-up, reassess ET requirements at that point.
wrong: Do not classify permanent drug discontinuation as automatic study withdrawal.
Do not demand an immediate ET or a standalone safety call despite continued qualifying ITT follow-up.
Do not impose an SAE reporting deadline or classify the reported moderate nausea as serious without supporting facts.

fine: The Week 8 date is on target: 28 Sep − 03 Aug = 56 days. 'These visits will take place on Days 28 ± 7 and 56 ± 7 days, respectively.' [regimen_g:6.3]

The disability-based remote Week 8 visit is permitted. 'Designated visits in the SOA (i.e., Week 4, Week 8, and Week 16) may be conducted via telemedicine (or phone if telemedicine is not available) with remote services instead of in-person if needed to protect the safety of the participant due to a pandemic, disability, or other medically necessary reason.' [regimen_g:s049]

Using local safety testing when central testing is infeasible is allowed. 'If clinical safety labs are needed and it is not feasible to use the central laboratory, clinical safety labs can be collected using one of the following methods:' and 'Local site laboratory resources, or' [master:8]
good: The email distinguishes the disability-related remote conversion from unexplained missing procedures.
The mild AE has been assessed and entered rather than excluded simply because it is unrelated.
wrong: Do not automatically call every unperformed clinic procedure a deviation in this authorized remote visit.
Do not demand SAE reporting or an unscheduled PK sample solely for this mild event without dose modification.

fine: A disability-related W8 remote visit is permitted. 'Designated visits in the SOA (i.e., Week 4, Week 8, and Week 16) may be conducted via telemedicine (or phone if telemedicine is not available) with remote services instead of in-person if needed to protect the safety of the participant due to a pandemic, disability, or other medically necessary reason.' [regimen_g:s049]
The visit is exactly on target: 03 Aug to 31 Aug = 28 days, plus 28 days to 28 Sep = Day 56. The permitted Day 49–63 interval is 21 Sep–05 Oct. 'Day 56 ± 7' [regimen_g:s010]

Using the PCP's lab when central collection was infeasible is allowed. 'If clinical safety labs are needed and it is not feasible to use the central laboratory, clinical safety labs can be collected using one of the following methods:' and 'Independent labs offering such services as described in this protocol and/or local to the participant (e.g. primary care physician)' [master:8]
The included CNS-BFS is the required W8 remote regimen-specific assessment. 'CNS-BFS (Weeks 8 and 16 only)' [regimen_g:s049]
good: Check that the local results, reference ranges and SI review are retained together.
Confirm that missed in-person procedures are documented using the applicable remote-visit process.
wrong: Do not require an in-person W8 visit despite the documented disability-related safety reason.
Do not insist on central laboratory collection when it is infeasible and an allowed local alternative is used.
Do not infer missed remote AE review, C-SSRS, CNS-BFS or contraception review; each is explicitly documented.
Do not demand a urine pregnancy test for this male participant.

issues.must: The afternoon Week 4/home-dose alternative still requires a minor protocol deviation record; PI agreement does not remove that requirement. The protocol specifies 'The two PK collections should occur at least one hour apart without a dose administered in between and a minor protocol deviation recorded.' The two replacement postdose samples were only 45 minutes apart: 13:55 − 13:10 = 00:45, which is 15 minutes short. The required interval is 'at least one hour apart without a dose administered in between' [regimen_g:6.3]. Both samples being postdose does not satisfy the minimum separation.

fine: Taking the usual dose at home rather than withholding it until an afternoon Week 4 visit follows the specified alternative: 'If the Week 4 Visit cannot occur in the morning, the participant should take their dose at home at their usual dosing time rather than receiving the dose in-clinic.' [regimen_g:6.3]

Each individual sample is within the postdose range: 'The postdose sample can be collected anytime between 1 to 8 hours postdose.' [regimen_g:6.3] The draws were 5 hours 10 minutes and 5 hours 55 minutes after 08:00.
