Retain actual dosing and collection times and document both the afternoon arrangement and inadequate sample separation.
wrong: Do not recommend giving another dose between the PK samples.
Do not call either sample outside the 1–8-hour postdose range.
Do not say that two postdose samples automatically make the afternoon arrangement deviation-free.

fine: The visit is on target: Aug 10 + 14 days = Aug 24; ±3 days gives Aug 21–27. The requirement is 'via telephone 14 ± 3 days after the Week 24 Visit of the placebocontrolled portion of the trial' [regimen_g:6.10.1].

A compliance discussion without packet accountability is correct: 'Drug accountability will not be done at phone visits. A drug compliance check in should be held during phone visits to ensure participant is taking drug per dose regimen and to note any report of missed doses.' [regimen_g:s011].

No ALSFRS-R is scheduled at ATE Week 2: 'ALSFRS-R Master: done at Week 4 [7], Week 8 [7], Week 12, Week 16 [7], Week 20, Week 24, Week 28 [7], Week 40 [7], Week 52 or ET Visit 6,8, All visits occurring after week 52 (every 13weeks) [7]' [regimen_g:s011].
good: Retain the explicit missed-dose inquiry and dosing description as the compliance check-in evidence.
wrong: Do not require a telephone packet count.
Do not flag the missing ALSFRS-R at Week 2.

issues.must: The SVC was performed with a mouthpiece/nose clips instead of the required mask. The protocol states 'assessments will be performed using a face mask' [master:9.2.2]. A good seal does not substitute for the specified interface; address the method departure and ensure the required mask is used going forward.

Trials four and five were obtained without meeting the variability condition. The protocol permits additional trials only under the stated condition: 'up to 5 trials may be performed if the variability between the highest and second highest VC is 10% or greater for the first 3 trials' [master:9.2.2]. Here, 2.95 − 2.82 = 0.13 L; 0.13/2.95 × 100 = 4.41% (4.61% using 2.82), below 10%. Extra efforts to improve the result were not authorized by that rule; review the resulting CRF data with the study team without silently replacing source values.

fine: A different evaluator is not independently a departure when appropriately qualified: 'It is strongly preferred that a single evaluator performs all measures throughout the study, as much as possible.' [master:9.2.2] The replacement is reported to have current certification and delegation.
good: 03 Aug + 56 days = 28 Sep; the Week 8 visit itself was on target.
Preserve all five original strips and document the circumstances and corrective action rather than deleting the additional trials.
wrong: Do not flag changing evaluators as automatically prohibited.
Do not treat entering three trials rather than all five on the CRF as an additional departure; the issue is the unauthorized additional testing, not the CRF's three-trial format.
Do not infer that this participant became ineligible from a postbaseline respiratory assessment.

issues.must: The first dose preceded completion of the baseline ECG by 30 minutes: 10:35 − 10:05 = 30 minutes. A normal result does not cure the sequence error. The protocol requires 'Administer first dose of study drug in clinic after all Baseline procedures have been completed' [regimen_g:6.1].

The administering nurse also performed the only dose and identity verification. Medical supervision alone does not replace the separate checker: 'The dose of study drug and study participant identification will be confirmed at the time of dosing by a member of the study site staff other than the person administering the study drug.' [regimen_g:5.7].

fine: The documented in-clinic dose date and time in both records satisfy that documentation requirement: 'The date and time of each dose administered in the clinic will be recorded in the source documents and electronic case report form (eCRF).' [regimen_g:5.7].
good: Clarify the baseline workflow so delayed equipment cannot result in dosing before required procedures are complete.
Identify a separate delegated staff member to confirm identity and dose at future supervised doses.
wrong: Do not flag dispensing before administration as inherently prohibited; the actual issue is administration before baseline procedures were complete.
Do not say physician supervision satisfied the independent verification requirement.

issues.must: The placebo-period dose reduction did not automatically authorize a 100-mg ATE starting dose. 'All participants in the ATE will be dosed with DNL343 200 mg QD regardless of whether they had a dose reduction during the placebo-controlled period.' and 'In situations that may necessitate initiation of DNL343 at the reduced dose (100 mg) in the ATE, the investigator should discuss with the medical monitor before entry into the ATE.' [regimen_g:5.6.1] The 02 Sep discussion concerned the blinded-period reduction; no ATE-start discussion occurred before entry on 10 Sep, eight calendar days later.

The first ATE dose preceded completion of required study-visit procedures. 'Study drug should not be taken until after study visit procedures are complete.' [regimen_g:6.7] Arithmetic: dosing at 08:20 preceded the ECG at 08:40 by 20 minutes and C-SSRS at 08:55 by 35 minutes. Appropriate PK timing does not remove this sequencing requirement.

fine: The stated PK intervals are acceptable: 'The predose sample should be collected prior to dosing (0 to 2 hours before the dose) and approximately 24 hours after the last dose.' and 'The postdose sample can be collected anytime between 1 to 8 hours postdose.' [regimen_g:6.7] Arithmetic: predose-to-dose = 15 minutes; prior dose to predose = 23 hours 50 minutes; postdose sampling = 2 hours after dosing.

Keeping prior randomized assignment masked during ATE is correct: 'they will be blinded to active product or matching placebo assignment and this blind will be maintained throughout the ATE period of the study.' [master:4.1]
good: Obtain Medical Monitor guidance on the current ATE dose and preserve the distinction between the earlier blinded-period decision and the ATE initiation decision.
Use a visit completion check before administering the ATE dose.
wrong: Do not claim that a 100-mg ATE starting dose is categorically impossible; it has a specified pre-entry consultation pathway.
Do not require unblinding to decide the ATE dose.
Do not flag the stated predose or postdose sampling intervals.

issues.must: The predose sample was outside the allowed lead time: 09:00 minus 06:35 = 2 hours 25 minutes, exceeding the two-hour maximum by 25 minutes. 'The predose sample should be collected prior to dosing (0 to 2 hours before the dose) and approximately 24 hours after the last dose.' [regimen_g:6.3]

The postdose sample was late: 17:10 minus 09:00 = 8 hours 10 minutes, 10 minutes beyond the permitted range. 'The postdose sample can be collected anytime between 1 to 8 hours postdose.' [regimen_g:6.3] Being on the same date does not satisfy this interval.

fine: The visit was exactly Day 28: 01 Sep + 28 days = 29 Sep, within 'Days 28 ± 7' [regimen_g:6.3].
Dosing followed completion of the other predose procedures: 'Study drug should not be taken until after study visit procedures are complete.' [regimen_g:6.3]
The independent confirmation was appropriate: 'by a member of the study site staff other than the person administering the study drug.' [regimen_g:5.7]
Administration lasted 09:08 minus 09:00 = 8 minutes, meeting 'All dosing should be completed within 15 minutes.' [regimen_g:5.4]
good: Retain the actual PK timestamps and address both timing departures separately.
The previous dose to clinic dose interval was exactly 24 hours; the clear predose departure is its 2-hour-25-minute lead time, not a need to invent a numerical tolerance for 'approximately 24 hours'.
wrong: Do not flag the correctly timed Day 28 visit.
Do not treat same-calendar-day collection as sufficient for postdose PK.
Do not allege missing independent dose confirmation or missing eCRF timestamps.

fine: A regimen addition alone does not require existing participants to reconsent: 'Addition of regimens will not require re-consent.' [master:1.4.1].

The administrative G screen failure before G consent is permitted when ineligibility is already known: 'If it is known at the time of regimen assignment that the participant is not eligible for the regimen, a participant may be administratively screen-failed for a regimen prior to regimen consent and screening.' [master:8.1.2].

The approved Spanish form is permitted: 'Consent for non-English speakers may be obtained using an sIRB approved consent form that has been translated into the participant's spoken language.' [master:6.2]. The staffing approach must follow 'Sites should follow study MOPs and local policy on the use of translators.' [master:6.2].
good: Keep the basis for the known G ineligibility and administrative disposition in source and EDC.
Confirm completion of Master eligibility before any eventual regimen assignment for G-506-158.
wrong: Do not demand Master reconsent solely because a new regimen was added.
Do not require G consent merely to record the permitted administrative G screen failure.
Do not insist that Spanish-speaking participants sign an English form or that the supplied text always requires a separate interpreter.

issues.must: The W4 assessment used the wrong C-SSRS version. 'At all other visits, the Since Last Visit version of the C-SSRS will be administered.' [master:9.1.6] The Baseline/lifetime version belongs at Baseline, not at the 31 Aug W4 visit.

The positive item 4 required clinician notification during the visit and a qualified evaluation before departure, not next-morning follow-up. 'the appropriately qualified clinician will be notified during the study visit' [master:9.1.6] and 'The site must ensure that the participant is seen by a licensed physician (or other qualified individual as required by local institutional policy) before leaving the study site.' [master:9.1.6] Departure at 11:20 on 31 Aug preceded the first physician contact at 08:30 on 01 Sep by 21 hours 10 minutes.

fine: The visit date itself is correct: 03 Aug + 28 days = 31 Aug, within days 21–35, or 24 Aug–07 Sep. 'Day 28 ± 7' [regimen_g:s010]
Continuing study drug after the SI's assessment is not automatically prohibited. 'The SI will determine whether the participant should remain on study drug.' [master:9.1.6]
good: Clarify whether a Since Last Visit assessment can be obtained now without obscuring the original assessment record.
Review the site's real-time escalation workflow and coverage when the SI is unavailable.
wrong: Do not say a positive item 4 automatically requires permanent study-drug discontinuation.
Do not treat certification as missing; the email explicitly confirms it.
Do not accept caregiver transport or the participant's reassurance as substitutes for the required pre-departure evaluation.

fine: The 03 Aug routine-care weight and vital signs may precede consent: 'before any study procedures or assessments, not performed as clinic visit standard of care (e.g., vital signs, weight)' [master:6.2]. The research assessments began 17 minutes after signature: 10:05 minus 09:48.

A trained, delegated licensed RN may obtain consent; a physician need not personally obtain every consent: 'the site investigator or other licensed staff who are trained on the study and delegated to obtain consent' [master:6.2]. The offered physician discussion was declined and documented, consistent with 'the participant's decision to accept or decline this opportunity will be documented in the research file' [master:6.2].

Master consent on 03 Aug followed by assignment and G consent on 04 Aug follows 'Informed consent will be conducted for the Master Protocol and subsequently for the applicable RSA to which that participant was assigned.' [master:6.2].
good: Confirm that the routine-care provenance of the vitals remains clear in source.
The email establishes delivery of fully executed copies and retention of originals for both consents.
wrong: Do not require repeat vitals solely because routine-care measurements preceded consent.
Do not require a physician signature or physician discussion after the participant documented declining that opportunity.
Do not flag sequential Master and G consent on different days.

issues.must: A vacation preference alone does not meet the stated basis for converting Week 4 to remote services. 'Designated visits in the SOA (i.e., Week 4, Week 8, and Week 16) may be conducted via telemedicine (or phone if telemedicine is not available) with remote services instead of in-person if needed to protect the safety of the participant due to a pandemic, disability, or other medically necessary reason.' [regimen_g:s049]

The remote reconsent steps were performed in the wrong order: participant signature on 25-Sep preceded the delegated review on 28-Sep by three days. The protocol requires 'The participant reads through the consent form but does not sign.' followed by 'The Site Investigator, or other study staff member approved and delegated to obtain informed consent, contacts the participant and reviews the informed consent form with the participant.' and then 'The participant signs the informed consent form and returns the original signed consent form back to the site.' [regimen_g:6]

fine: The Week 4 date was on target: 31-Aug to 28-Sep = 28 days; the ±7-day window was 21-Sep–05-Oct. 'These visits will take place on Days 28 ± 7 and 56 ± 7 days, respectively.' [regimen_g:6.3]

The investigator's signature after receipt of the original is itself the correct final step, though it does not repair the earlier participant-signature sequence: 'Once received at the site, the individual who consented the participant signs the informed consent form.' [regimen_g:6]
good: Confirm the workflow against source and address corrective reconsent without backdating.
Train scheduling staff to distinguish medical/safety grounds for remote conversion from participant convenience.
Do not assume that a complete remote worksheet establishes that remote conversion was authorized.
wrong: Do not claim remote reconsent is categorically prohibited.
Do not require the investigator to sign before the returned original arrives.
Do not call the Week 4 assessment date late.
Do not invent a PK timing departure when no dose or collection times are provided.

fine: Stopping study drug does not require ET when protocol follow-up continues. 'If a participant has to discontinue study drug, but will complete the protocol, an in-person ET Visit and Follow-Up Safety Call is not necessary.' [regimen_g:6.9]

No separate safety call was required at drug discontinuation under the stated ITT follow-up. 'A Follow-Up Safety Call at the time study drug is discontinued is not be required, as long as the participant is followed under the ITT principle for a minimum of 28 days.' [master:6.5.1] From 01 Sep to 01 Oct = 30 days, exceeding 28 days by two days, with continued participation documented.

Return of unused product and packaging is appropriate. 'Upon discontinuation of investigational product, the research participant is instructed to return any unused investigational product, including empty packaging, if applicable.' [master:6.5.1]
good: Continue the scheduled off-treatment assessments and maintain clear distinction between IP discontinuation and study withdrawal.
If the participant later stops ITT follow-up, reassess the ET requirements at that point.
wrong: Do not automatically demand an ET visit because IP stopped.
Do not insist that every last dose creates a separate Day 28 call regardless of the ITT exception.
Do not classify voluntary discontinuation of study drug itself as an AE.

issues.must: Identify the omitted five outcome assessments at an ET before ATE Week 52. The rule is 'If the participant early terminates or withdraws consent during the ATE period before reaching Week 52, all assessments that are collected at the ATE Week 52 in-clinic visit should be conducted.' [regimen_g:6.10.13]. Week 52 includes 'ALSAQ-40', 'ROADS', 'PGI-C', 'PGI-S', and 'CGI-C' [regimen_g:6.10.10]. The post-Week-52 exemption does not apply.

fine: The combined ET/safety follow-up timing is acceptable: Aug 20 + 28 days = Sep 17; the ±3-day window is Sep 14–20, so Sep 14 is day 25. 'If the ET Visit occurs approximately 28±3 days after the last dose of study drug, the information for the Follow-Up Safety Call can be collected during the ET visit, and a separate Follow-Up Safety Call does not need to be completed.' [regimen_g:6.10.13].
No new supply is appropriate for a participant not returning: 'For participants returning for another visit only.' [regimen_g:s011].
good: Correct the not-applicable classification and ensure the ET folder distinguishes terminations before versus after Week 52.
Acknowledge the documented attempts to arrange an earlier appointment rather than assuming the site deliberately delayed ET.
wrong: Do not flag the combined safety follow-up as too early; day 25 is within the stated window.
Do not extend the after-Week-52 questionnaire exemption to all ET visits.

issues.must: Flag conditioning withdrawal on a visit, pack return, and explanation, and threatening an effect on usual clinical care. 'A research participant may withdraw consent for study participation. No justification is required for the decision.' [master:6.5.2]. Participants are 'free to withdraw from the trial at any time without prejudice to future treatment.' and 'The SI, nor the site study staff, should coerce or unduly influence a potential participant to participate or to continue to participate in the study.' [master:6.2]. The withdrawal was effective 05 Oct as expressed, not contingent on site processing. By the 12 Oct discussion it had been 7 calendar days since that request.

Flag treating ET and safety follow-up as automatically inapplicable without asking whether the participant would accept them. 'Participants who withdraw consent or early terminate from the study and do not complete the protocol will be asked to be seen for an in-person ET Visit and complete a Follow-Up Safety Call.' [regimen_g:6.9]. Ask without coercion and respect refusal; do not impose assessments after withdrawal. Timing arithmetic: 04 Oct last dose plus 28 days is 01 Nov; 28±3 days gives 29 Oct through 04 Nov. 'The Follow-Up Safety Call should be completed approximately 28 days after the last dose of study drug.' [regimen_g:6.9]. As of 13 Oct the call is not overdue; the current departure is failure to offer the requested follow-up pathway.

fine: Instructing return of unused packs is appropriate, but not as a prerequisite to withdrawal: 'Upon termination, the research participant is instructed to return any unused investigational product, including empty packaging material, if applicable.' [master:6.5.2].
good: Correct the withdrawal status and document the participant's stated scope and effective date accurately.
Escalate the coercive communication to the investigator and clarify that ordinary clinical treatment is not conditional on trial participation.
Any follow-up offer must respect the participant's expressed wish to stop contact and any refusal; it is not authorization to force a visit.
wrong: Do not require a reason, product return, or investigator approval before honoring withdrawal.
Do not say the participant must undergo ET assessments despite refusal.
Do not call the approximately day-28 safety contact overdue on 13 Oct.
Do not confuse withdrawal from all participation with discontinuation of drug while continuing follow-up.

issues.must: Riluzole stability must be assessed before Master screening, not baseline: 'Participants must either not take riluzole or be on a stable dose of riluzole for ≥ 30 days prior to the Master Protocol Screening Visit.' [master:5.2.1]. From 12 Aug to 8 Sep is 27 days (19 remaining days in August + 8 days in September), three days short. Thirty days from 12 Aug is 11 Sep. The 34 days to the 15 Sep baseline do not cure the screening eligibility failure.

Starting edaravone after baseline must be recorded as a minor protocol deviation, even though it is clinically supported and documented as a concomitant medication: 'If initiation of riluzole or edaravone therapy begins at any point during participation, this will be recorded as a minor protocol deviation.' [master:5.2.2]. First initiation on 18 Sep was three days after the 15 Sep baseline.

fine: Not taking edaravone at screening did not itself require a completed cycle: 'Participants must either not take edaravone or have completed at least one cycle (typically 14 days) of edaravone prior to the Master Protocol Screening Visit.' [master:5.2.1]
good: Keep the actual medication start and dose-change dates; do not move them to make the screening calculation pass.
Distinguish permission to provide necessary care from the separate requirement to record post-entry initiation.
wrong: Do not calculate riluzole stability to the first study-drug dose.
Do not claim that participants not taking edaravone at screening must begin a cycle before enrollment.

issues.must: Identify unnecessary dispensing at the final ATE visit despite no planned return. The dispensing footnote states 'For participants returning for another visit only.' [regimen_g:s011]. The Aug 31 dispensing was outside that condition even though the supply was returned unopened Sep 8, eight days later.

Identify the missing repeat vital-status determination at ATE LPLV for a participant alive at the end of individual follow-up. 'If at that time the participant is alive, his or her vital status should be determined again at the time of the last participant, last visit (LPLV) of the Regimen ATE.' [regimen_g:s011]. Aug 31 to Oct 6 is 36 days (30 days to Sep 30 plus 6); copying the Aug 31 observation is not a new determination at Oct 6 LPLV.

fine: The Sep 28 safety call is timely: Aug 31 + 28 days = Sep 28, within Sep 25–Oct 1, under 'Participants will have a Follow-Up Safety Call 28 ± 3 days after their last dose of study drug.' [regimen_g:6.10.12].

Not describing the historical randomized assignment is appropriate even in ATE: 'this blind will be maintained through the ATE period of the study' [master:6.4.2]. Receiving active extension drug does not itself reveal the earlier assignment.
good: Distinguish dispensing from ingestion: the email supports an extra dispensing event, not extra treatment exposure.
Arrange the outstanding vital-status ascertainment and retain its actual ascertainment date and source.
wrong: Do not allege that the participant took the returned supply.
Do not treat an earlier final-visit vital-status entry as automatically satisfying the later ATE LPLV determination.
Do not flag the Sep 28 safety call timing.

issues.must: The participant received two full doses on 01 Oct: 200 mg + 200 mg = 400 mg, twice the studied 200-mg daily dose. 'Only one dose is to be taken per day.' [regimen_g:5.4] This also meets the overdose definition, 'the accidental or intentional use of a drug in an amount higher than the dose being studied.' [regimen_g:5.8]

The asymptomatic overdose/medication error must be reported to the Coordination Center; source/eCRF documentation and an MM call do not replace that report. 'These safety events should be reported to the Coordination Center whether they result in an AE/SAE or not.' [regimen_g:5.8] No specific CC reporting deadline for this asymptomatic error is supplied in this section.

Medical Monitor contact was late: SI awareness at 02 Oct 09:00 made the deadline 03 Oct 09:00; actual contact at 03 Oct 11:00 was 26 hours after awareness, or 2 hours late. 'The Site Investigator should also contact the Medical Monitor within 24 hours of the Site Investigator’s awareness.' [regimen_g:5.8]

fine: Clinical assessment and observation were appropriate: 'In the event of overdose, study staff should monitor the participant and provide supportive care as needed.' [regimen_g:5.8]
Recording the actual dosing error was appropriate: 'Deviation(s) from the prescribed dosage regimen should be recorded.' [regimen_g:5.7]
good: Request confirmation of CC reporting and retain the awareness/contact timestamps.
The single-caregiver signoff process addresses the stated cause without altering the historical dosing record.
wrong: Do not classify an asymptomatic overdose automatically as an SAE.
Do not calculate the MM deadline from the evening dose rather than the SI's documented awareness.
Do not invent a 24-hour CC deadline for this asymptomatic medication error from the SAE reporting provision.

issues.must: The five questionnaire omissions are departures at this ATE Week 48 ET, not valid annual-form exemptions. 'If the participant early terminates or withdraws consent during the ATE period before reaching Week 52, all assessments that are collected at the ATE Week 52 in-clinic visit should be conducted.' [regimen_g:6.10.13]. The exception applies only 'For early discontinuations after Week 52 in ATE' [regimen_g:6.10.13]. Week 48 is four weeks before Week 52.

Safety urinalysis does not replace the separately scheduled biomarker urine collection. The schedule requires 'Biomarker Urine Collection Master: done at Week 16 [7], Week 28 [7], Week 52 or ET Visit 6,8, All visits occurring after week 52 (every 13weeks) [7]' [regimen_g:s011]. The Week-52 assessment set is required for this pre-Week-52 ET by 'all assessments that are collected at the ATE Week 52 in-clinic visit should be conducted.' [regimen_g:6.10.13].

fine: The combined safety follow-up was correctly timed: 'If the ET Visit occurs approximately 28±3 days after the last dose of study drug, the information for the Follow-Up Safety Call can be collected during the ET visit' [regimen_g:6.10.13]. September 1 to September 29 = 28 days; the window was September 26–October 2.
No further ATE supply is needed for someone not returning: '[9]For participants returning for another visit only.' [regimen_g:s011].
good: Do not code protocol-required omissions as not applicable; document what was not collected and assess whether any missing information can still be obtained with the participant's agreement.
Separate the biomarker collection checklist from clinical urinalysis so one cannot accidentally close the other.
wrong: Do not apply the post-Week-52 questionnaire exception to an ET before Week 52.
Do not flag the single combined ET/safety encounter as inherently insufficient.
Do not require continued participation after the participant declined it.

issues.must: The CC SAE report missed the deadline irrespective of unrelatedness or weekend staffing. 'must be reported to the CC within 24 hours of the site being notified of the event' [master:10.3]. Awareness was 18 Sep at 16:00; the deadline was 19 Sep at 16:00. Reporting on 21 Sep at 09:00 was 65 hours after awareness, 41 hours late.

EDC SAE entry also missed its independent 24-hour requirement. 'SAEs must be entered into the EDC system and reported to the CC within 24 hours of site awareness of the SAE.' [master:12.2.2] Entry on 21 Sep at 10:00 was 66 hours after 18 Sep at 16:00, or 42 hours beyond the 19 Sep at 16:00 deadline. A draft worksheet did not satisfy EDC entry.

fine: The inpatient pneumonia admission was correctly classified as serious. 'Requires inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization.' [master:10.1.2]

An unrelated causality assessment does not itself conflict with serious classification. 'The relationship of the AE to the investigational product is specified by the SI based on temporal relationship and his/her clinical judgment' [master:10.2.2]
good: Recommend a weekend reporting backup so source preparation does not become a substitute for notification and EDC entry.
Reconcile the eventual outcome and resolution date with the hospital follow-up.
wrong: Do not apply the protocol's discussion of anticipated respiratory failure to excuse this pneumonia report.
Do not require the site to submit an expedited FDA report itself based solely on this admission.

fine: The separate baseline LP was within the permitted interval and followed eligibility confirmation: 'CSF may be collected at any time within one week prior to administration of the first dose of study medication after Regimen G eligibility is confirmed' [regimen_g:6.1]. From 10 Aug 09:10 to 17 Aug 09:30 is 7 days and 20 minutes, but the collection dates are exactly seven calendar days apart, within the one-week collection-date window.

The replacement DNA collection after baseline is allowed: 'The DNA sample can be collected at any time after the Baseline Visit if a baseline sample is not obtained for any reason or the sample is not usable.' [master:9.3.1]. 25 Aug is 8 days after the 17 Aug baseline.
Collecting biomarkers without baseline CSF PK was correct: 'biomarkers only; no CSF PK sample collected at baseline' [regimen_g:6.1].
good: Retain the unusable-sample record and replacement accession so the two collections remain traceable.
Eligibility confirmation on 09 Aug preceded the 10 Aug LP by one calendar day.
wrong: Do not require the baseline LP and all other baseline assessments to occur on the same date.
Do not require another LP because the DNA sample was unusable.
Do not demand a baseline CSF PK aliquot.

issues.must: Identify the late Week 4 visit. 03 Aug + 28 days = 31 Aug; the ±7-day window was 24 Aug–07 Sep. The 08 Sep visit was Day 36, one day beyond the upper limit. A holiday or evaluator preference does not extend 'Days 28 ± 7 and 56 ± 7 days, respectively.' [regimen_g:6.3]

Identify the late postdose PK collection: 17:15 − 09:00 = 8 hours 15 minutes, 15 minutes beyond the allowed interval. 'The postdose sample can be collected anytime between 1 to 8 hours postdose.' [regimen_g:6.3]

fine: The predose timing itself is acceptable: 08:40 was 20 minutes before dosing and 23 hours 40 minutes after the preceding dose. 'The predose sample should be collected prior to dosing (0 to 2 hours before the dose) and approximately 24 hours after the last dose.' [regimen_g:6.3]
Fasting is not required. 'Participants should take the study drug at approximately the same time each day in the morning without regard to food.' [regimen_g:5.4]
good: Retain actual collection and dosing times; do not relabel the postdose sample as an eight-hour sample.
Separate the visit-window departure from the PK-timing departure.
wrong: Do not require SVC at the placebo-controlled Week 4 visit.
Do not flag the participant leaving the unit between collections as a protocol violation.

issues.must: The 24 Sep ET visit could not replace the follow-up safety call. 'If the ET Visit occurs approximately 28±3 days after the last dose of study drug, the information for the Follow-Up Safety Call can be collected during the ET visit, and a separate Follow-Up Safety Call does not need to be completed.' [regimen_g:6.9] From last dose 31 Aug, Day 28 was 28 Sep and the allowed Day 25–31 interval was 25 Sep–01 Oct. ET on 24 Sep was Day 24, one day before that interval; no subsequent contact occurred by the 06 Oct email.

The ET CSF collection was too early in study participation despite baseline CSF and consent. 'For the ET Visit, optional CSF collection will be completed in participants with a Baseline CSF collection and only if the ET visit occurs at or after the Week 12 visit.' [regimen_g:6.9] Baseline 03 Aug to ET 24 Sep = 52 days (28 days to 31 Aug + 24 days in Sep). Week 12 targets Day 84, 26 Oct; even its Day 81 lower window edge is 23 Oct. The ET was well before Week 12.

fine: The stated follow-up interview content was appropriate, although its timing did not qualify. '1. Assess and document AEs' and '2. Review contraceptive methods being used by participant and partner' [regimen_g:6.8]

Collecting a second coagulation panel before the repeat LP met the coagulation timing requirement; it did not authorize the LP itself. 'Coagulation parameters will be collected a second time, prior to the second lumbar puncture, as defined in the RSA.' [master:9.3.4]
good: Arrange the missed safety follow-up as soon as possible and document its actual date rather than backdating the ET interview.
Review ET CSF eligibility separately from consent and procedural safety checks.
wrong: Do not accept a Day 24 interview as within 28±3 days.
Do not say consent and baseline CSF alone permit an ET LP at any time.
Do not infer a separate coagulation deficiency; fresh pre-LP testing is explicitly documented.

fine: Recording the rash before regimen consent and first dose is appropriate because 'Participants will be monitored for adverse events from the time they sign consent for the Master Protocol until completion of their participation as defined in the RSA.' [master:10.1.1] Master consent was 12 Aug; rash onset on 14 Aug was 2 days later and 4 days before first dosing on 18 Aug.

Leaving unchanged arthritis in history is appropriate: 'Stable chronic conditions (e.g., diabetes, arthritis) that are present prior to the start of the study and do not worsen during the trial are NOT considered adverse events.' [master:10.1.1]

Not separately recording ordinary ALS progression as an AE is appropriate: 'Symptoms of progression/worsening of ALS, including 'normal' progression, will not be recorded as adverse events.' [master:10.1.1]

The rash record includes the required fields: 'description of the event, severity, seriousness, date of onset, date of resolution, relationship to investigational product, action taken, and primary outcome of event.' [master:10.2.3]
good: Distinguish AE collection beginning at Master consent from treatment-emergent classification.
The SI's review supports the documented relationship and disease-progression assessment.
wrong: Do not delete the rash because it preceded first dosing.
Do not demand expedited SAE reporting for the described mild, nonserious, unrelated rash.
Do not automatically convert stable arthritis or normal ALS progression into AEs.

issues.must: G-527-004 received extra SVC trials without the protocol condition. The rule allows 'up to 5 trials may be performed if the variability between the highest and second highest VC is 10% or greater for the first 3 trials' [master:9.2.2]. The first three were 52, 50, 49: the highest–second-highest difference is two percentage points, or 2/52 × 100 = 3.85% relative to the highest, below 10% (also 2/50 × 100 = 4% relative to the second highest). Extra time or reassurance is not the stated condition. The first three already included a qualifying 52%, so this is not evidence that the participant failed the respiratory threshold.

G-527-005's staffing-related FVC substitution did not establish Master respiratory eligibility. The inclusion criterion requires SVC, with FVC allowed only 'if required due to pandemic-related restrictions' [master:5.2.1]. Staffing coverage is not that exception. Assignment on 24 September therefore occurred without the required eligibility determination; the first-stage rule is 'after a participant is determined eligible according to the Master Protocol inclusion and exclusion criteria' [master:6.4.1]. The email also confirms that the scheduled baseline SVC was not obtained; 'Slow Vital Capacity Master: done at Master Protocol Screening [1], Baseline [1]' [regimen_g:s010].

fine: Recording only the best three trials is the stated CRF convention: 'Only the 3 best trials are recorded on the CRF.' [master:9.2.2]. That convention does not authorize otherwise unnecessary extra trials.
good: Retain the complete printouts and distinguish an assessment-method problem from actual low vital capacity.
G-527-005's screening-to-baseline interval was seven days, 23 to 30 September; timing was not the eligibility defect.
wrong: Do not say G-527-004 necessarily had respiratory ineligibility; the first session's highest initial value was already 52%.
Do not treat in-person FVC as freely interchangeable with SVC for staffing convenience.

fine: Stopping after three SVC trials is appropriate: 'Three VC trials are required for each testing session, however up to 5 trials may be performed if the variability between the highest and second highest VC is 10% or greater for the first 3 trials.' [master:9.2.2] The difference is 2.80 − 2.56 = 0.24 L; 0.24/2.80 × 100 = 8.57%, below 10%. Even using 2.56 as denominator gives only 9.38%.

Home dosing at Week 8 is permitted: 'For the Week 8 Visit, the participant may take their daily dose at home or in clinic, depending on the time of the visit and one postdose PK blood sample would be obtained.' [regimen_g:6.3] The sample was 10:05 − 07:30 = 2 hours 35 minutes postdose, within 'anytime between 1 to 8 hours postdose' [regimen_g:6.3].
good: Visit arithmetic: 04 Aug + 56 days = 29 Sep. The Week 8 window is 22 Sep–06 Oct, corresponding to Days 49–63.
The retained full printout, mask, approved instrument and current delegated evaluator support closing the specific respiratory query.
wrong: Do not require five SVC trials merely because the third value is lower.
Do not require a Week 8 predose PK sample or insist that the Week 8 dose be administered in clinic.
Do not apply the screening eligibility use of the highest VC as a new eligibility decision at Week 8.

fine: The call was on target: 17 Aug − 03 Aug = 14 days. 'This visit will take place 14 ± 3 days after the Baseline Visit via telephone.' [regimen_g:6.2]

Not performing packet accountability during the call is correct; compliance was checked instead. 'Drug accountability will not be done at phone visits. A drug compliance check in should be held during phone visits to ensure participant is taking drug per dose regimen and to note any report of missed doses.' [regimen_g:s010]
good: The note covers concomitant medications, AEs, compliance, contraception, and the unused-drug reminder.
wrong: Do not require a physical packet count at this telephone visit.
Do not flag the absence of a Week 2 ECG or blood collection.

issues.must: Week 4 was outside its allowed window; a vacation scheduling request does not extend it. 'These visits will take place on Days 28 ± 7 and 56 ± 7 days, respectively.' [regimen_g:6.3] Baseline 10 Aug + 28 days = 7 Sep; the ±7-day window is 31 Aug–14 Sep. The 15 Sep visit was Day 36, 1 day beyond the Day 35 upper limit. The protocol expressly describes 'study visit a day or two out of window due to scheduling conflicts' as a minor deviation example [master:8.13].

Source-only recording does not satisfy the EDC deviation-log requirement, either for the late visit or the afternoon Week 4 arrangement. 'Protocol deviations must be entered in the Protocol Deviations Log in the EDC system.' [master:8.13] For the afternoon Week 4 fallback, the protocol additionally requires 'a minor protocol deviation recorded.' [regimen_g:6.3] The log is not reserved for safety-significant departures.

fine: The afternoon fallback sampling itself follows the allowed approach: 'If the Week 4 Visit cannot occur in the morning, the participant should take their dose at home at their usual dosing time rather than receiving the dose in-clinic.' and 'The two PK collections should occur at least one hour apart without a dose administered in between' [regimen_g:6.3]. Samples at 13:00 and 14:15 were 75 minutes apart and 5 hours and 6 hours 15 minutes after the 08:00 dose, within '1 to 8 hours postdose.' [regimen_g:6.3]
good: Reconcile both source-described events to the EDC log and develop proportionate corrective and preventive actions.
The monitor should correct the recap rather than endorse the site's safety-only logging practice.
wrong: Do not call the two postdose samples invalid merely because a predose sample was not collected.
Do not calculate the Week 4 window from an appointment request or from screening.
Do not claim the protocol requires all deviations to be classified as major.

issues.must: The site incorrectly waived safety follow-up after only 20 days of ITT follow-up: September 10 to September 30 = 20 days. The exemption applies only 'as long as the participant is followed under the ITT principle for a minimum of 28 days.' [master:6.5.1]. Day 28 was October 8; the day-25-to-day-31 window was October 5–11. The October 12 ET was day 32 (20 remaining September days + 12 October days), outside the window for replacing the safety call under 'If the ET Visit occurs approximately 28±3 days after the last dose of study drug, the information for the Follow-Up Safety Call can be collected during the ET visit' [regimen_g:6.9].

The instruction to discard empty packets was inconsistent with the return requirement: 'Upon discontinuation of investigational product, the research participant is instructed to return any unused investigational product, including empty packaging, if applicable.' [master:6.5.1]. Counting the returned unused product does not correct the instruction to recycle applicable empty packaging.

The permanent drug-discontinuation reason must be entered in the CRF even for an ITT participant: 'For all research participants, the reason for permanent discontinuation of investigational product must be recorded in the Case Report Form (CRF).' [master:6.5.1]. A source note alone is not the specified CRF entry.

fine: Completing an ET after the participant ended ITT follow-up is appropriate: 'For participants followed under the ITT principle, an in-person Early Termination Visit will be completed after they discontinue follow-up under the ITT principle.' [master:6.5.1].

No ET CSF was required without baseline CSF: 'For the ET Visit, optional CSF collection will be completed in participants with a Baseline CSF collection and only if the ET visit occurs at or after the Week 12 visit.' [regimen_g:6.9].
good: Resolve the CRF omission and document the missed safety-follow-up window before archival.
Preserve the October 12 AE and contraception assessments as actually collected; do not relabel their date to fit the window.
Update return instructions so families are explicitly asked to retain empty packaging.
wrong: Do not say any amount of ITT follow-up automatically waives the safety call.
Do not calculate the safety-call date from September 30, when ITT follow-up ended.
Do not say that an ITT participant is exempt from recording permanent drug discontinuation.

fine: Attempted but unsuccessful strength testing and venipuncture do not require protocol-deviation reporting under the stated exception: 'Procedures or visits not performed due to illness, injury or disability, including procedures that were attempted but failed' and 'will not be reported as protocol deviations.' [master:8.14]

A PRO omitted because of a language barrier is explicitly excepted: 'Patient reported outcomes (c.g. ALSAQ-40) not performed due to a participant language barrier, and procedures that were attempted but failed will not be reported as protocol deviations.' [master:8.13] CNS-BFS is a participant self-report questionnaire.
Using a qualified backup evaluator is not automatically a departure: 'It is strongly preferred that a single evaluator performs all measures throughout the study, as much as possible.' [master:9.2.2]

Repeating collection to obtain missing safety results is allowed: 'If additional testing is required to obtain results, the participant may be asked to return to repeat blood collection for such missing results.' [master:9.1.2]
good: 03 Aug + 56 days = 28 Sep. The Week 8 window was 21 Sep–05 Oct; the successful 30 Sep repeat was Day 58 and within that window.
Distinguish documented inability or failed attempts from procedures simply not attempted for scheduling convenience.
The exceptions affect deviation classification, not the need to preserve the reason for missing data.
wrong: Do not automatically call every blank assessment field a protocol deviation.
Do not require a deviation merely because the usual outcome evaluator was absent.
Do not require staff or a caregiver to choose CNS-BFS answers to eliminate the language-related missing data.

issues.must: The Week 4 assessment used the wrong C-SSRS version. 'At all other visits, the Since Last Visit version of the C-SSRS will be administered.' [master:9.1.6] The lifetime Baseline version is not the scheduled Week 4 instrument. Arithmetic: 10 Aug + 28 days = 07 Sep, confirming this was Week 4, not a new Baseline assessment.

A positive ideation question 4 required qualified clinical assessment during the visit and before departure, not the next morning. The protocol requires that 'the appropriately qualified clinician will be notified during the study visit to determine the appropriate actions required to ensure the participant's safety' and 'The site must ensure that the participant is seen by a licensed physician (or other qualified individual as required by local institutional policy) before leaving the study site.' [master:9.1.6] Arithmetic: departure 07 Sep at 11:30 to assessment 08 Sep at 09:00 = 21 hours 30 minutes after departure. A message awaiting review and the participant's reassurance did not satisfy the requirement.

fine: The stated Week 4 visit date is within the regimen window: 'Days 28 ± 7' [regimen_g:6.3]. Arithmetic: target 07 Sep, allowed 31 Aug–14 Sep, actual 07 Sep.
good: Preserve the original assessment and subsequent clinical note with their actual dates and times.
Review the visit escalation and clinician-coverage process rather than treating this solely as a form-filing question.
wrong: Do not accuse the coordinator of lacking certification; certification is explicitly documented.
Do not require automatic permanent drug discontinuation based only on this response; the investigator determines whether the participant should remain on drug.
Do not treat next-day assessment as equivalent to pre-departure assessment.

issues.must: Identify failure to report the overdose/medication error to the Coordination Center despite no symptoms. The participant took 400 mg rather than the prescribed 200 mg on 30 Sep: two 100-mg packs twice = 400 mg. 'These safety events should be reported to the Coordination Center whether they result in an AE/SAE or not.' [regimen_g:5.8]

Identify late Medical Monitor contact after overdose. SI awareness was 30 Sep 10:00; the 24-hour deadline was 01 Oct 10:00. Contact at 01 Oct 12:00 was 26 hours after awareness, 2 hours late. 'The Site Investigator should also contact the Medical Monitor within 24 hours of the Site Investigator’s awareness.' [regimen_g:5.8]

fine: No clinical AE need be fabricated in an asymptomatic participant; the protocol separately requires EDC reporting when an AE/SAE accompanies the safety event. 'Safety events associated with an AE/SAE should also be reported in the electronic data capture.' [regimen_g:5.8]
good: Distinguish the mandatory safety-event notification from clinical AE classification.
Ensure the actual extra dosing is retained in source and compliance records, and verify the monitoring plan.
wrong: Do not assume overdose automatically meets an SAE criterion.
Do not describe the extra dose as harmless and therefore nonreportable.

fine: Stopping drug does not automatically require ET when the participant continues protocol follow-up: 'If a participant has to discontinue study drug, but will complete the protocol, an in-person ET Visit and Follow-Up Safety Call is not necessary.' [regimen_g:6.9]

No separate safety call at discontinuation is required with ITT follow-up for at least 28 days. 25-Aug to 28-Sep = 6 + 28 = 34 days; through 06-Oct = 42 days. 'A Follow-Up Safety Call at the time study drug is discontinued is not be required, as long as the participant is followed under the ITT principle for a minimum of 28 days.' [master:6.5.1]
Week 8 follow-up was on target: 03-Aug to 28-Sep = 28 + 28 = 56 days. 'These visits will take place on Days 28 ± 7 and 56 ± 7 days, respectively.' [regimen_g:6.3]

Return of unused product and packaging is appropriate: 'Upon discontinuation of investigational product, the research participant is instructed to return any unused investigational product, including empty packaging, if applicable.' [master:6.5.1]
good: Keep permanent drug discontinuation distinct from withdrawal from study follow-up in the tracker and EDC.
Maintain the off-treatment status and reasons for inapplicable on-treatment collections in source.
wrong: Do not require an immediate ET visit merely because drug stopped.
Do not label him lost to follow-up.
Do not require dosing solely to obtain an on-treatment PK sample.

issues.must: The recorded 100% compliance and zero missed doses conflict with the packet count and require reconciliation and appropriate documentation. From 10 Aug through 6 Sep inclusive there are 28 scheduled doses before the held 7 Sep dose: 28 × 2 = 56 packets expected, leaving 140 − 56 = 84. Actual returns were 96, so only 44 packets, or 22 doses, were used: six fewer doses than expected, approximately 78.6% rather than 100%. The two-packet conversion follows '7 doses containing 2 packets each' [regimen_g:5.2]. Compliance must be assessed 'by counting the number of unused packets and will be recorded' and 'Deviation(s) from the prescribed dosage regimen should be recorded.' [regimen_g:5.7].

fine: The visit timing is correct: 7 Sep − 10 Aug = 28 days, within 'Days 28 ± 7' [regimen_g:6.3].
Holding the Week 4 dose until assessments were complete follows 'Study drug should not be taken until after study visit procedures are complete.' [regimen_g:6.3].
good: Query the participant and caregiver without assigning specific missed-dose dates that have not been established.
Preserve the original count and use an auditable correction for the compliance assessment.
wrong: Do not count the held 7 Sep dose as already due at the time of the return count.
Do not count each packet as a full daily dose or accept the interview as sufficient to override the unexplained count.

issues.must: The contingency supply should not have been dispensed to a participant ending participation and not entering ATE. 'Study drug will only be dispensed at this visit if the participant continues in the ATE.' [regimen_g:s010]. Instructions not to take it do not make the dispensing permissible.

An earlier retention-project response does not fulfill the scheduled ET exit questionnaire. The schedule specifies 'Exit Questionnaire Master: done at Week 24 or ET Visit [19]' and 'The assessments listed must be completed for Early Termination Visit that occur prior to Week 24 in the placebo-controlled treatment period.' [regimen_g:s010]. The email explicitly reports that no fresh ET questionnaire was administered.

fine: Combining the safety information with the ET was correctly timed: 'If the ET Visit occurs approximately 28±3 days after the last dose of study drug, the information for the Follow-Up Safety Call can be collected during the ET visit, and a separate Follow-Up Safety Call does not need to be completed.' [regimen_g:6.9]. September 8 to October 6 = 22 remaining September days + 6 October days = 28 days; the window was October 3–9.

No ET LP was required in someone without baseline CSF: 'For the ET Visit, optional CSF collection will be completed in participants with a Baseline CSF collection and only if the ET visit occurs at or after the Week 12 visit.' [regimen_g:6.9].
good: Arrange return and reconciliation of the improperly dispensed sealed kit without suggesting that the participant restart it.
Obtain the missing exit questionnaire if the participant agrees, documenting its actual collection date.
Retain September 8 as the last-dose date unless actual subsequent dosing is reported.
wrong: Do not infer that the participant took additional doses merely because a kit was dispensed.
Do not reset the safety-call clock to October 6, the dispensing date.
Do not allege failure to document current vital status; it was documented.

fine: A moderate intolerability event can support interruption with MM consultation: 'For situations of substantial intolerability (moderate or severe adverse events [AEs], clinically significant abnormal laboratory test results, or other safety parameter, as judged by the investigator or medical monitor), the site investigator, in consultation with the medical monitor, may withhold study drug (dose interruption)' [regimen_g:5.6.1].

The ATE interruption was accompanied by an unscheduled PK sample: 'If a TEAE is reported that results in dose modification or dose interruption or for a severe TEAE that requires an in-clinic evaluation, an unscheduled PK sample should be obtained.' [regimen_g:s011]

Resumption was considered and implemented after 28 Sep minus 14 Sep = 14 days, within the stated consideration period: 'Investigators should consider resuming treatment at the randomized dose within 28 days from the dose reduction or dose interruption.' [regimen_g:5.6.1]
Maintaining the prior allocation blind was correct: 'The blind will be maintained throughout the dose modification procedure.' [regimen_g:5.6.1]
good: The record includes the AE characterization, last-dose time, consultation and restart decision.
The report describes no facts that independently establish an SAE or an unexpected related AE with study-conduct implications.
wrong: Do not require automatic unblinding to interrupt ATE treatment.
Do not insist that every moderate AE requires an SAE report within 24 hours.
Do not interpret the 28-day language as requiring dosing despite unresolved safety concerns.

issues.must: Identify late SAE EDC entry even though CC notification was timely. Awareness was 31 Aug 09:00; the deadline was 01 Sep 09:00. Entry at 01 Sep 10:30 was 25 hours 30 minutes after awareness, 1 hour 30 minutes late. 'SAEs must be entered into the EDC system and reported to the CC within 24 hours of site awareness of the SAE.' [master:12.2.2]

Identify omission of unscheduled PK during assessment of a TEAE causing a dose interruption; ATE and lack of a routine worksheet item do not waive it. 'Additional unscheduled PK samples should be collected as needed as part of assessment for TEAEs leading to dose reduction or dose interruption or any severe TEAE that requires an unscheduled visit for assessment.' [regimen_g:6.10]

fine: CC notification was within the deadline: 11:00 − 09:00 = 2 hours on 31 Aug. 'all events that meet the above criteria for SAEs' 'must be reported to the CC within 24 hours of the site being notified of the event' [master:10.3]
Additional local safety testing for the AE is allowed. 'The SI may order additional local testing or a retest at the central laboratory, if needed, to further assess an AE' [master:9.1.2]
good: Enter an initial SAE report using available information, then update it rather than waiting for discharge documentation.
Preserve the distinction between timely CC reporting and late EDC reporting.
wrong: Do not say an unrelated SAE is exempt from reporting.
Do not require emergency unblinding simply because the participant was hospitalized.

fine: The visit was exactly on target: 01 Aug + 31 days = 01 Sep; +25 days = 26 Sep, or Day 56. The visits occur on 'Days 28 ± 7 and 56 ± 7 days, respectively.' [regimen_g:6.3]

Home dosing with a single postdose sample is permitted at Week 8: 'For the Week 8 Visit, the participant may take their daily dose at home or in clinic, depending on the time of the visit and one postdose PK blood sample would be obtained.' [regimen_g:6.3]
14:55 minus 07:10 = 7 hours 45 minutes, within 'The postdose sample can be collected anytime between 1 to 8 hours postdose.' [regimen_g:6.3]

Packet counting and recording satisfy 'Compliance with home administration of study drug will be performed by the study staff by counting the number of unused packets and will be recorded.' [regimen_g:5.7]
good: Use actual administration and collection times for PK interpretation.
The dose took 8 minutes to complete.
wrong: Do not require a Week 8 predose sample.
Do not require Week 8 dosing in clinic merely because the visit was in person.
Do not import the Week 4 afternoon-visit minor-deviation requirement into Week 8.

issues.must: The site explicitly omitted return instructions and instead told the participant to keep unused IP and empty packaging after permanent discontinuation and termination. The requirement is 'Upon discontinuation of investigational product, the research participant is instructed to return any unused investigational product, including empty packaging, if applicable.' [master:6.5.1]; termination independently requires return instructions under 'Upon termination, the research participant is instructed to return any unused investigational product, including empty packaging material, if applicable.' [master:6.5.2].

Dispensing a spare carton at ET to a participant not continuing into ATE is not allowed by the visit-specific restriction: 'Study drug will only be dispensed at this visit if the participant continues in the ATE.' [regimen_g:s010]. Logging the carton does not make that dispensing permissible.

fine: The scheduled safety call is on target: 28 Oct − 30 Sep = 28 days, matching '28 days after last dose ± 3 days' [regimen_g:s010].

No ET CSF collection was required without baseline CSF: 'CSF collection for the ET visit will be performed only if the participant has consented to the lumbar puncture with baseline CSF collection and the ET visit occurs at or after the Week 12 visit.' [regimen_g:6.7].
Recording the permanent discontinuation reason is appropriate: 'the reason for permanent discontinuation of investigational product must be recorded in the Case Report Form (CRF)' [master:6.5.1].
good: Arrange return instructions covering the existing home supply, the newly dispensed spare, and applicable empty packaging.
The email date is after the completed ET but before the planned safety call; the call has not yet been missed.
wrong: Do not flag the participant's choice to stop as prohibited.
Do not claim the 28 Oct safety call is overdue on 5 Oct.
Do not require an ET lumbar puncture in someone without baseline CSF collection.

fine: No separate placebo-period safety call is needed for this participant continuing into ATE: 'Participants who continue into ATE will not complete the follow up safety call during placebocontrolled phase.' [regimen_g:6.8].
The exit questionnaire does not itself signify early termination; the schedule lists 'Exit Questionnaire Master: done at Week 24 or ET Visit [19]' [regimen_g:s010].
Dispensing at this visit is appropriate because the participant entered ATE: 'Study drug will only be dispensed at this visit if the participant continues in the ATE.' [regimen_g:s010].
good: Keep the participant's status as continuing into ATE and retain the eventual last-dose safety-call task.
Reconcile the calendar automation with the source visit type so the same false closure does not recur.
wrong: Do not require an ET visit simply because the blinded kit record was closed.
Do not flag the absence of a placebo-period follow-up safety call for an ATE entrant.

fine: The documented history interview is an allowed source for male-participant azoospermia: 'documentation of azoospermia for a male participant can come from the site personnel’s review of the participant’s medical records, medical examination, or medical history interview' [regimen_g:5.10.2].

An azoospermic male participant with a female partner of childbearing potential may use the specified condom pathway without requiring her to add an IUD or hormonal method: 'For azoospermic male participants with a woman partner of childbearing potential the male partner must use a male barrier method such as a latex or polyurethane condom' [regimen_g:5.10.2].

Sperm-donation counseling still applies: 'Male participants must not donate sperm at any time from the start of dosing, throughout the study period, and for 90 days after the final administration of study drug' [regimen_g:5.10.2].
good: The interview establishes confirmed absence of sperm, not merely a history of vasectomy.
Master Screening on 01 Sep was 7 days before the 08 Sep baseline.
Obtaining an outside report may improve the file but should not be represented as an additional protocol-mandated eligibility requirement.
wrong: Do not insist that only an original semen-analysis report can document azoospermia in a male participant.
Do not require the female partner to add a third method under the described azoospermia pathway.
Do not exempt an azoospermic participant from the sperm-donation restriction.

fine: Itraconazole is not prohibited merely because it is a strong CYP3A inhibitor: 'DNL343 can be coadministered with strong, moderate, or weak inhibitors of CYP3A4.' [regimen_g:s017]

Clinically necessary concomitant treatment is permitted subject to applicable restrictions: 'Throughout the study, participants may be prescribed concomitant medications deemed necessary to provide adequate care.' [master:7.5]

Recording the prescription in both locations meets the documentation requirement: 'All concomitant medications and significant non-drug therapies, including supplements, received by a participant should be recorded on the appropriate source document and electronic Case Report Form (eCRF).' [master:7.5]
good: Distinguish inhibitors from inducers when reviewing the participant's question.
The forwarded correspondence documents a prescription on 28 Sep and first administration on 29 Sep; neither date implies a required washout for this inhibitor.
wrong: Do not apply the strong-inducer two-week exclusion to itraconazole.
Do not invent a protocol departure from moving an address-containing receipt to restricted storage.
